title: CHILmesh: a fast 2D mesh library for triangular, quadrilateral, and mixed-element grids

creators.name: Kubatko, Ethan J.
creators.affiliation: Computational Hydrodynamics & Informatics Laboratory, The Ohio State University

description:
CHILmesh is a Python toolkit for two-dimensional triangular, quadrilateral and mixed-element meshes, designed so the meshes it builds and edits can be used by hydrodynamic models such as ADCIRC. It reads and writes ADCIRC mesh, forcing and output files, SMS .2dm and Gmsh files, peels a mesh into element layers from the boundary inward, smooths nodes with FEM, angle-based and truss smoothers, and reports element quality. The layer method follows the QuADMESH+ thesis (Mattioli, 2017). An optional prebuilt C++ backend runs full initialization 8.6 to 14.7 times faster than pure Python. Install with pip install chilmesh (pip install "chilmesh[cpp]" for the C++ backend); the import name is chilmesh.

This release (1.7.0)

Changed

  • Licence text replaced by the official PolyForm text, with separate no-AI terms (#308).
  • Benchmark documentation corrects the degree-of-freedom figures and the speedup range (#304).
  • Python 3.10 support is removed: requires-python is now >=3.11. Version 1.6.x remains installable on 3.10.

Fixed

  • fort.14 open-boundary IBTYPEE is kept on read and written back, so a read, write, re-read round trip compares equal (#309).
  • angle_based_smoother rejects any quad move that folds a corner; quad smoothing output may differ from 1.6.x (#306).
  • partition_mesh and partition_report build mesh adjacencies on demand (#293).

Roadmap at 1.7.0

  • Now: a native .chil container format (#201); benchmarks against competing mesh libraries (#301).
  • Next: MCP server tools (#286); a streaming GPU mesh view (#167); a full-lifecycle benchmark on the STOFS-2D-Global mesh (#276).
  • Later: one ecosystem with ADMESH and QuADMESH.
